newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia will not cut imports on rupiah-report.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia will not cut imports on rupiah-report.

text.p: Indonesia will not reduce imports of commodities such as sugar, wheat flour and soybeans despite a sharp decline of the rupiah against the U.S. dollar, the official Antara news agency reported on Monday.

Beddu Amang, head of the national logistics bureau (BULOG), was quoted as saying currency fluctuations would not affect the agency's imports. "BULOG's efforts to maintain the stability of domestic prices is not linked with prices abroad," he said.
Antara said BULOG had imported around 2.7 million tonnes of wheat flour so far this year, and that its annual sugar imports totalled some 600,000 tonnes.
BULOG has an import monopoly on sugar, soybeans, flour and rice.
The rupiah has weakened by some 20 percent against the U.S. dollar so far this year.
